subject: Order form + MSA: questions on usage tiers, tax jurisdiction, and payment terms
messages:
From: Sarah Halpern <sarah@orbitiq.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form & MSA - initial questions about usage tiers and tax

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week — excited to move OrbitIQ onto Redwood for inference serving. Procurement asked me to surface a few items before we hand off to legal:

1) Usage tiers / overage handling: the order form we received includes tiered monthly units with an automatic billing increment at 20% overage. Can you confirm how overages are calculated (rolling vs. peak) and whether we can add a brief SLA credit if tokens exceed the committed tier?

2) Tax jurisdiction: OrbitIQ is headquartered in NY with customers in multiple states. We need to confirm whether taxes will be applied based on buyer location or Redwood's billing address.

3) Payment terms: procurement prefers Net-60. Is there flexibility?

I've attached our PO (OrbitIQ_PO_8792.pdf) and a filled order-form draft (OrbitIQ_orderform_draft.xlsx) for reference.

Can you route this to your contracts team and let me know the best time for a short call to align on these items?

Thanks,
Sarah Halpern
Sr. Procurement Manager | OrbitIQ
Attachments: OrbitIQ_PO_8792.pdf, OrbitIQ_orderform_draft.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Sarah Halpern <sarah@orbitiq.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form & MSA - initial questions about usage tiers and tax

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending these over. Looping in Kimberly from Legal for redlines and Jonas for billing.

Quick answers & next steps:
- We track overages on a monthly rolling basis (consumption beyond the committed monthly units). That said, we can discuss a modest service credit model for sustained overage events on the call.
- Taxes are normally applied by buyer jurisdiction; I want Legal to confirm any nuances for multi-state remittance.
- Net-60 is longer than our standard Net-30 for new customers, but we can discuss options (e.g., Net-45 or a short-term Net-60 with early-pay incentive).

Kimberly — can you review the attached OrbitIQ orderform and the PO, and flag any MSA/orderform language we should preemptively propose? Suggested agenda for a 30-min sync: usage/overage calc, tax treatment, payment term, and which MSA template to use.

I can do a call tomorrow (Aug 30) 9–11 PT or 2–4 PT. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa / Sarah — quick read of the materials attached. I did a first-pass of the MSA and order form and flagged the following items that will likely require commercial discussion:

1) Taxes (Section 7): we need confirmed buyer-jurisdiction treatment in writing. If OrbitIQ requires seller to collect based on customer location for all downstream customers, that creates administrative burden and may require a tax indemnity.

2) Indemnity & Cap (Section 9): Redwood proposes a standard liability cap tied to fees; OrbitIQ’s procurement language references a higher threshold. Need to know if they will accept the cap or request exceptions for IP claims.

3) Overages and SLA credits (Order Form Attachment): if they want an SLA-based credit for over-usage, we should define criteria (sustained >20% for 2 consecutive months) and a clear credit formula to avoid open-ended exposure.

4) Data residency / export control (Section 12): confirm whether OrbitIQ has any EU/UK residency requirements for any portion of data; if so, we need to match hosting region or include carveouts.

5) Payment terms (Exhibit B): Net-60 is outside standard. If Procurement needs Net-60, request a limited approval and escalate for finance sign-off. Jonas — can you advise on whether billing can accept Net-60 with ACH/PO?

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_comments_kim_20250829.docx (first-pass comments inline).

From a process perspective, if OrbitIQ is comfortable using Redwood’s MSA we can prepare a tracked-redline with a short cover memo. If they insist on their vendor form, we’ll need to map any material deviations.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Halpern <sarah@orbitiq.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, procurement@orbitiq.com
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form & MSA - initial questions about usage tiers and tax

Marissa / Kimberly,

Thanks for the thorough review. A few clarifications from Procurement here:

• Tax: OrbitIQ requires taxes be applied based on buyer/customer location (we remit sales/use taxes per state for our customers). For the Redwood billing relationship, OrbitIQ will remit any sales taxes due for its purchases based on our NY headquarters, but we cannot accept responsibility for downstream customer tax collection.

• Overages: We cannot accept a caps-only approach that limits credits to 1% of fees when overages are material to our business. We can accept a negotiated credit schedule (for example: 10% credit for sustained 20–50% overage; 25% credit for sustained >50% overage), but need to discuss thresholds and proof of sustained usage.

• Payment terms: Procurement prefers Net-60 and will push for it. If Redwood is willing to offer Net-60 for initial year with a 1.5% early-pay discount for Net-30, that would be acceptable as a compromise.

Attached is our vendor form (OrbitIQ_vendor_form_filled.pdf). We’re OK using Redwood’s MSA if Redwood can send a tracked-redline that incorporates the credit schedule and payment term proposal.

Let us know a call time tomorrow (Aug 31 PT) — Sarah is available 9–11 PT, procurement team available 10–12 PT.

Best,
Sarah Halpern
Sr. Procurement Manager | OrbitIQ
Attachments: OrbitIQ_vendor_form_filled.pdf
